worst_P_items.problem: Strongest edge artifact in either set. Every rooftop and building wall has a thick black contour line and flat posterized fills, so the city looks like a cel-shaded cartoon. Tree crowns have dark rims with bright lime-green tops. The drop-tower column and Ferris wheel spokes carry hard dark/white outline pairs, which is ringing.

An oil-paint or edge-detect filter look. Each tree crown is drawn with a dark contour line. The roller-coaster rails and supports have bright white halo strokes along their edges, and the tower body and base rings have heavy dark outlines. The P1_full frame looks like a painting, not camera footage.

Over-sharpened clouds. Thin cloud wisps are broken into many hard-edged shards and flecks that look like flying debris or birds, and each fragment has a crisp dark/light edge. Soft vapor gradients have turned into crunchy micro-contrast.

Tree canopy crowns have dark outline rings and exaggerated local contrast that look like stippling. The drop-ride frame and coaster have bright edge strokes. The hillside reads as a texture pattern, not foliage.

Building edges show dark outlining with a slight bright fringe, and tree crowns are rimmed. The effect is milder than P1/P6 but clearly over-sharpened. P5 and P7 are the only clean frames in set P: they are slightly soft with no notable halos.

worst_Q_items.problem: Crunchy, over-sharpened foliage with high micro-contrast on the conifer crowns. The roller-coaster rails have bright, glowing edge lines, and the image looks saturated and sharpened. There are no black contour outlines like those in P1/P6.

A thin bright halo runs along the tower outline and antenna where they meet the blue sky, with slight ringing on the diagonal struts. The sky clouds have somewhat hard bright edges. Q3_ground_right also has smeared, melted-looking rooftops, which is generation smear rather than sharpening.

Tree crowns on the hill have exaggerated light-top/dark-gap micro-contrast that looks crunchy. A few sky wisps are slightly fragmented (Q2_sky, left side). This is moderate over-sharpening, not cartoon outlines.

The tower edges and struts are crisply sharpened with a faint light fringe. Building edges in the ground crops show mild halos combined with softness and smear. Overall this is moderate and closer to typical upscaled footage.

result.summary: Lens: edge halos and over-sharpening. Set P is clearly worse. Four of its seven frames (P1, P2, P3, P6) have severe artifacts: dark contour lines around every tree crown and building, which give a cel-shaded or oil-paint look in P1 and P6 especially, white halo strokes along the coaster rails and tower edges, and clouds broken into crunchy hard-edged shards (P3, P4, P6 sky). P4 is moderate. Only P5 and P7 look like natural, slightly soft camera footage. Set Q is also over-sharpened, with crunchy foliage micro-contrast, bright rail edges in Q1/Q2, and a faint light halo around the tower against the blue sky in Q3/Q4. None of the Q frames shows the black-outline posterization or shattered-cloud artifacts that dominate P. Q is cleaner overall but still not fully natural.

worst_P_items.problem: Worst frame of either set. It looks like a cartoon or toon filter. Each building is reduced to flat grey or cream shapes with thick black ink outlines on the roof edges (ground_left upper half, ground_right throughout). Each tree crown in ground_left has a hard dark contour and a bright rim, like broccoli. The sky is full of small torn-paper flakes and comma-shaped specks scattered between the clouds, and cloud edges are frayed and crunchy. It reads as a painting, not camera footage.

Oil-paint or posterized look. In ground_right the whole hillside is traced with black outlines around every tree clump, giving an etched, engraved texture, and the high-rises have dark halos. In ground_left the trees are clumped broccoli blobs with dark contours, and the roller coaster rails have glowing edge halos. In the sky the clouds break into speckled, flaky fragments, and dozens of loose flake specks are scattered across the clear sky on the right.

The sky is very crunchy. The clouds dissolve into jagged, feathered flakes, like shredded paper or bird flocks, across the whole upper area. The trees are broccoli clumps with dark outline strokes. The buildings in ground_right have bright edge halos and posterized shading.

The tree canopy is painted as outlined brush blobs with dark contour lines between crowns. This is strongest in ground_right, where the whole slope looks like a stroke filter. The sky has crunchy, flaky cloud edges and speckle in the lower clouds.

The sky clouds break into jagged flake fragments, worst on the upper right. In ground_left the trees are uniform broccoli domes with dark rims and a bright top highlight, which looks painterly. Buildings are moderately clean but oversharpened. P5 and P7 by contrast are fairly natural, soft and clean, with only faint flaking at the upper-left of the sky in P5.

worst_Q_items.problem: The trees are oversharpened and stylized. The conifer clumps have crisp dark separations and a plasticky, saturated sheen, and in ground_left the canopy forms broccoli domes. The roller coaster rails have orange glow halos. The sky has several patches of flaky, bird-like cloud wisps on the left. The look is lighter than P1, without the full black ink tracing, but it is still clearly processed.

Same treatment as Q1. The trees are broccoli clumps with bright rim highlights and a plastic sheen, and the slope in ground_right has crunchy dark gaps. The sky has some flaked or torn cloud fragments at the left and center. It is less extreme than the matching P frames.

The buildings in ground_right are smeared and melted. The rooftops run together into waxy, rounded blobs with no clear edges, especially in the middle and right, so it reads as mush. The tower in the center crop has a stray black squiggle, like a bird shape, drawn across the window band at upper left. The sky is clean.

The same black squiggle artifact appears on the tower's window band at left. The roof clusters at the top right of ground_right are slightly smeared and blobby, and the clouds have mild sharpening halos. Otherwise this is the most natural frame in Q.

result.summary: Lens: texture realism. Set P is badly split. P5 and P7 look soft and natural, but P1, P2, P3, P4 and P6 show a heavy painterly or posterized treatment. Tree crowns are traced with dark ink outlines and look like broccoli. Clouds break into crunchy, torn-paper flakes scattered across clear sky. P6 is worst: the buildings themselves are toon-shaded with black outlines. That is 5 of 7 frames failing badly, so P scores 3.5. Set Q still has over-processing. Q1 and Q2 have sharpened, plasticky broccoli trees and some flaky cloud wisps, but without P's full black edge-tracing. Q3 and Q4 have clean skies, though Q3 has melted, smeared rooftops and both show a black squiggle artifact on the tower windows. Q scores 5.5. Q is cleaner overall, but neither set consistently looks like clean real camera footage.

worst_P_items.problem: Heavy posterization that looks like a cel-shaded or cartoon filter. Every building in the city has a dark ink-like outline, and the flat surfaces are reduced to a few tones. Tree crowns look like stamped blobs with dark rims. P6_sky.png has dozens of small dark smudge-flakes scattered across a smooth sky. Nothing in this frame looks like camera footage.

Strong oil-paint, over-sharpened look. Tree clumps on the hill have dark contour halos and look painted rather than photographed, and the coaster rails have bright ringing edges. In P1_sky.png the clouds are broken into ragged, outlined flake clusters with debris spread over the right half of the sky. In P1_ground_right.png the apartment blocks carry a dark edge halo against the sky.

The sky is full of smeared, torn cloud fragments that look like a warp or interpolation artifact. Dark comma-shaped streaks trail off the main cloud to the right. P3_ground_right.png has painterly tree texture with edge darkening, and the buildings have crunchy, haloed edges.

The same painterly tree texture as P1: each canopy has dark outlines, and the hill looks brush-stroked. The roller-coaster and drop-tower legs have bright ringing. The sky is cleaner, but cloud edges are slightly speckled.

Crinkled, torn cloud edges, with flake debris at the upper right of the sky crop. Tree crowns in ground_left have mild dark rims. The city in P4_ground_right.png is fairly crisp, so P4 is moderate rather than severe.

These are the cleanest frames in either set and look closest to real footage. Remaining flaws: mild upscale softness and slightly waxy or smeared building facades and tree canopies, and a few small smudge-flakes in the P5 sky at the upper left.

worst_Q_items.problem: Looks upscaled from low resolution. Small houses and roofs are mushy and melted together, and windows and cars are smeared into blobs. Over-sharpening halos sit on top of the soft detail. Q3_center.png also has a strange dark wing-shaped mark printed on the tower's panel band. The sky is clean, with no banding.

The same soft, upscaled look as Q3. Facade windows on the apartment towers are smeared, roof detail is waxy, and the edges have sharpening halos. The same dark mark appears on the tower panel in Q4_center.png. The sky is clean.
At the left of the sky crop, clouds break into wispy fragments with dark speckles. Trees are over-sharpened with a slightly crunchy, painted look, though much milder than in P1.
A few fragmented, smudged cloud wisps at the left and center of the sky. Trees are slightly over-sharpened, but the coaster rails are clean, with no notable aliasing. This is the cleanest Q frame.

result.summary:
I viewed all 11 full frames and all 44 crops. I found no meaningful compression blocking or sky banding in either set, and thin structures like antennas, guy wires and coaster rails show little aliasing. The main defects come from AI generation or enhancement: painterly or posterized textures, dark contour halos, fragmented cloud debris, and soft, smeared detail.

Set P is very uneven. P1 and P6 have severe cartoon-filter posterization: buildings are outlined, trees look stamped, and the skies are full of flakes. P2 and P3 have a strong oil-paint look on trees, and P3's sky has smeared, torn cloud streaks. P4 is moderate. P5 and P7 are fairly clean, close to real footage, with only mild softness.

Set Q is more consistent. Q1 and Q2 are crisp with mild over-sharpening and a few fragmented cloud wisps. Q3 and Q4 have clean skies, but the ground detail is soft and smeared, as if upscaled from low resolution with halos added. They also share an odd dark mark on the tower panel. Q's worst problem is softness, which is less objectionable than P's posterization.

Q is cleaner overall. Neither set fully reads as clean, natural 4K camera footage, because both show visible processing artifacts at 100% crop.
